scope: Existing reader adds two application-side information-loss cases; no new input-system article.

sources.author: SDL contributors
claims: Current keystate and queued event history are different data.
Key state is updated before the internal path attempts event posting.
PollEvent retrieves a queued event, not a rewind of the current state array.
limits: Pinned source reading does not verify live SDL, OS or device behavior.
Event posting is conditional; example assumes accepted events fully delivered to the application.
No claim that every DOWN is observed after release, or that every PollEvent call repumps all devices.

novelty.existing_coverage: Fixed-step reader already covers short-press loss, repeat policy, tick assignment, zero-step retention and single consumption. Related layout, cancellation and combat-buffer material serves different boundaries.
new_value: Current-state recheck can discard an already queued short press.
Latched Boolean preserves at least one occurrence but merges two occurrences.
novelty.decision: Two bounded representation examples in existing reader only; no separate support or new book.

original_data_check.script: 管理档案/实验/输入事件表示/verify_event_reduction.py
observations: No events: held false, pressed false, zero requests.
Short press: held false, pressed true, one request.
Two short presses: held false, pressed true, two ordered requests.
Held with repeats: held true, pressed true, one request.
Using final false to gate the earlier DOWN discards the short-press request.
original_data_check.policy: Initially unheld; pressed_seen false at interval start, set by nonrepeat DOWN and not cleared by UP. One request per nonrepeat DOWN.
original_data_check.limits: Four supplied data sequences, not hardware acquisition, event-queue completeness, SDL execution or game simulation.

execution_limits: No SDL library, OS/device event collection, engine, game or human test.
No device-time to simulation-tick mapping or guaranteed action execution.
Original script reads no files, devices, credentials or network.
